id_and_class.summary: Andrew Downing Hartford argues that if anything ever exists, something always existed, since nothing comes from absolute nothing. This single eternal Source grounds everything, including our first-person consciousness, and because a minded Domain cannot come from a mindless Source, he concludes the Source itself is Minded.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness Grounded in an Eternal Minded Source

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Our consciousness is mindedness participating in the Domain of a single, eternal, Minded Source, the ‘always-existor’.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not emergent; from the standpoint of a Source that is first and last, nothing emerges, and evolution describes only events in ‘the middle’.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Phenomenology that is actual in the Domain, consciousness included, cannot arise from a Source in which it is absent.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: One necessary, unique, uncaused, unchanging always-existor that is neither physical, mathematical, nor computational, and a single Domain dependent on it.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: A priori reasoning from the first principle that ‘always’ must be satisfied by at least one base case. Because the always-existor cannot be observed or proven, each person must decide the question of Something versus Nothing axiomatically.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: The Source is both first and last in one eternal instance, at once ‘a-categorical’ (no defined object) and ‘all-categorical’ (the ground of every category). Only what is possible in the Source can be possible in us.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: The origin and grounding of first-person consciousness
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: A new reading of ‘always’ as prior to time: eternity is distinct from past and future time, which are concepts from the middle. Necessity, uniqueness, and invariance together yield one eternal Source and one Domain.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: We exist in the Source's single Domain, between its first and last instance.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The Source has no space and no quantum information, so it is no computer, and since it precedes all time it is no algorithm.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Evolution and the growth of complexity are real but limited in scope: they cannot explain the uncaused Source, which did not evolve or emerge.
core_claims_and_evidence: If there is ever Something, there always was Something, because no existence comes from absolute Nothing.
There can be only one always-existor, and it is both before and beyond all time.
A minded Domain cannot be separated from its Source, so the Source must be Minded.
A Minded Source that is not computational undercuts the assumption that computation produces consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: A priori metaphysical argument (an ‘a-cosmological’ first-principle argument).

empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Hartford grants that the always-existor cannot be observed or proven. He also leaves open whether artificial consciousness lies among all possibilities.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Hartford contrasts his argument with cosmological arguments: it does not reason backward from the world to a first cause but starts from ‘always’ as the base case.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since the Source of consciousness is not computational, Hartford sees no reason to expect computers to be conscious, though he says it remains to be seen.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: All existence, including our minds, belongs to the Domain of one eternal Minded Source, which Hartford sets against claims that the universe is meaningless.
